REQUEST_ID_COLUMN_FIRST.definition: provider request id = an id the LLM provider mints per HTTP request (Anthropic `request-id` response header, value `req_...`) that the harness stores in the log. Detected in the IR request_id column and by a raw-text key scan for request-id-like JSON keys (REQ_KEY_RX in the probe) in every corpus.

INTERPRETATION_verdict.headline: Provider request ids exist in exactly two of our seven corpora, and only one of them is public: SWE-chat's Claude Code raw transcripts. cc_local is private. Both are the same harness (Claude Code) and the same provider (Anthropic). The request-id mechanism therefore runs on one public harness/provider pair. It cannot be shown to transfer across harnesses or providers with the data we hold.
INTERPRETATION_verdict.coverage_bound: Within swechat, Claude Code calls carry a request id at 0.980 (session-clustered CI [0.973, 0.987]). Across all swechat harnesses it is 0.888 [0.862, 0.909], because Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Copilot carry none. Across every public tool call we hold (non-H) it is 380,855 of about 2.86 M, under 14%. That figure is descriptive, since aiv_cu dominates the denominator and counts calls per turn.
INTERPRETATION_verdict.decodable_time: Every request id we hold decodes under the inferred UUIDv7 layout: 305,727/305,727 in swechat and 35,379/35,379 in cc_local, with version and variant bits matching too. The layout is inferred, not documented: Anthropic's docs describe the header but not its structure, and one of the two example ids on that page does not decode. This is a material limitation for the design.
INTERPRETATION_verdict.nearest_substitutes: aiv_cu carries provider RESPONSE ids with embedded time: Gemini responseId and OpenAI Responses item ids at 1 s resolution, and Anthropic msg_ ids at ms resolution only after the 2026-07-06 switch (294,075 of 856,394). But aiv_cu stamps a turn once, so there is no input-to-first-output window to bracket. aiv_cc's msg_ ids carry no time.
gaps_that_cap_coverage: Bedrock-backed Claude Code calls carry no request id (0 of 3,575 non-H swechat calls); OpenAI-compatible proxies (msg_datetime14, chatcmpl) carry none either.
1,766 first-party Anthropic calls in swechat Claude Code lack a request id (382,061 - 380,295), and 246 raw `requestId` values are null.
SWE-chat's documented parquet tables drop the field; any pipeline built on conversations.parquet loses request ids.
